title: metric-roots-and-trace-collection-guide
content:
Purpose:
This is a working guide that ties metric 'roots' (canonical metric names/labels) to trace instrumentation and practical dashboard panels for fast root-cause debugging of inference latency and correctness regressions. Focus: developer-friendly signals for tokenized inference pipelines (hosted + dedicated + private).

Scope and goals:
- Provide a small, stable set of metric roots that teams can rely on across services (serving runtime, router, preproc, postproc, kvcache).
- Define span conventions and attributes so traces link cleanly to metrics and dashboards.
- Recommend sampling and tail-sampling rules that keep high-value traces while bounding storage costs.
- Layout a compact dashboard playbook optimized for debugging degraded P95/P99 latency, token stalls, and fallback events.

Design principles (short):
- Low-cardinality metric roots, high-cardinality attributes: keep time-series manageable by limiting label explosion on metrics; push extra dimensions to traces and logs.
- SLO-first: design metrics so they can be easily aggregated into SLOs (error_rate, latency buckets, throughput).
- Trace-to-metric links: every high-impact metric increase should point to a traceable operation with stable span names/attributes.
- Incrementally adopt: new services should implement a minimal subset and then add more attributes as needed.

Canonical metric roots (recommended names):
- inference.requests.count: counter (one per inbound inference request)
  - labels: route, model_name, model_variant, customer_tier, region
- inference.request.duration_ms: histogram (buckets: [10,30,50,100,250,500,1000,2000,5000])
  - labels: route, model_name, model_variant, gpu_type
- inference.tokens.generated.count: counter
  - labels: model_name, model_variant, route, prompt_type
- inference.kvcache.hit_ratio: gauge (0..1)
  - labels: model_name, model_variant
- inference.batch.size: histogram (buckets: [1,2,4,8,16,32,64])
  - labels: route, model_variant
- inference.encode.duration_ms: histogram (small buckets)
- inference.decode.duration_ms: histogram
- inference.rpc.error_count: counter
  - labels: kind (timeout, connection, server_error), service_name
- inference.fallback.count: counter (when request routed to lower-cost/compatible model)
  - labels: from_model, to_model, reason
- inference.cold_kvcache.count: counter (when kvcache misses cold-start)

Label guidance (keep low-cardinality):
- model_name: use canonical short id (e.g., "rw-gt-7b-v1"); avoid freeform commit hashes.
- model_variant: quantized/int8/int4 or fp16; allow "compat_v1" style.
- route: logical API route (e.g., "completion.v1", "chat.stream").
- prompt_type: enum: {system_only, short, long_prompt, zero_shot, few_shot}.
- customer_tier: {free, standard, enterprise}.

Metric naming anti-patterns:
- Avoid putting request_id, trace_id, or customer_id on metrics. Those belong in traces/logs.
- Don’t create one metric per model version and per deployment region unless necessary; instead use labels with small cardinality.

Span naming and attributes (tracing):
- Stable span name set (ordered path):
  1) http.inbound.receive  (attrs: http.method, route, client_ip_masked)
  2) request.route.resolve   (attrs: route, routing_decision, routed_to
     label: {pool:dense|sparse|fallback})
  3) preprocess.prompt.build (attrs: prompt_type, prompt_tokens)
  4) kvcache.lookup          (attrs: kvcache_hit:true|false, kvcache_latency_ms, kvcache_key_count)
  5) model.forward           (attrs: model_name, model_variant, batch_size, seq_len, gpu_type, flops_est)
  6) token.emission          (attrs: tokens_generated, streaming:true|false)
  7) postprocess.serialize  (attrs: payload_bytes, compress)
  8) http.outbound.respond   (attrs: status_code, response_size)
- For nested operations inside model.forward, prefer events instead of many spans: emit span events like "kernel_launch", "kv_fetch", "attention_compute" with timestamps. That reduces span-cardinality while retaining timing points.
- Always attach trace_id/span_id and the B3/W3C headers to outbound calls so other services can rejoin traces.

Trace attributes to push into logs (correlation):
- trace_id, span_id, request_id (X-Request-Id), model_name, model_variant, route, customer_tier.
- Example HTTP header propagation: "x-request-id", "traceparent" (W3C), "x-b3-traceid" (if used).

Sampling policy (practical):
- Default head-based sample rate: 1% for successful requests.
- Always keep: errors (status >= 500), timeouts, fallback events, kvcache cold misses, and any request with latency > p95_threshold (dynamic).
- Use tail-sampling: keep all traces where associated metrics show an outlier within a short window (e.g., if inference.request.duration_ms p95 > threshold for 1m, sample all traces for that route for next 5m).
- Priority sampling tags: add attributes like "telemetry.priority=high"
